findings.title: Exhausted federated recovery codes never removed
findings.body: After a successful recovery-code login the code fetches the credential via RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential() which can now return a federated user-storage credential, but cleanup still calls removeStoredCredentialById(). That API only removes a locally stored (Keycloak DB) credential and does not call UserStorageProvider/CredentialInputUpdater.disableCredentialType. Consequence: when recovery codes live in user storage an exhausted set is never deleted, isConfiguredFor stays true, and the user is not correctly forced through re-configuration.

findings.title: Federated storage cannot disable/remove recovery codes
findings.body: disableCredentialType() only handles OTP types and logs recovery-codes as unsupported, and getDisableableCredentialTypesStream() never advertises RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.TYPE. Consequence: even if production code tried the correct federated removal path (disableCredentialType), this provider would leak the credential, and account/admin removal flows cannot work for user-storage recovery codes. The test double therefore hides the production cleanup bug.

findings.title: Federated recovery-code validation does not consume codes
findings.body: isValid() for RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.TYPE just does anyMatch on the stored raw list and returns true without marking the used code as consumed/removed. The real RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialProvider marks a code used on validation so allCodesUsed() can become true. Consequence: federated codes are infinitely reusable in the test double, allCodesUsed() never becomes true, and the exhaustion / re-configure path added in RecoveryAuthnCodesFormAuthenticator is never exercised.

findings.title: Unchecked Optional.get() on missing recovery credential
findings.body: Constructor does RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential(user).get() with no isPresent check before createFromCredentialModel and getNextRecoveryAuthnCode().get(). If the user has no federated or local recovery credential the bean throws NoSuchElementException, producing a 500 during login-form rendering instead of a handled error. Someone reading only this finding understands: always check the Optional and fail gracefully.
